- When sentiment is consistently negative (e.g., >70% negative values), model tends to overcorrect downward; reduce forecast bias by 5–10% below historical mean.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior 7-day high), model often overshoots; cap forecast peak at 1.2x prior high or 1.5x 14-day moving average.
- If sentiment shows strong bullish momentum (e.g., 3+ consecutive +1.00), model frequently overestimates; apply downward bias of 3–5% to 30-day forecast.
- When sentiment is mixed or neutral (e.g., 50% ±1.00), model tends to lag; adjust forecast to align with 14-day moving average or 30-day median.
- If model forecast is >10% above true outcome for 3+ consecutive days, apply mean reversion correction: subtract 1.5–2.0% per day until convergence.
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome is consistently below 80% of model’s 1st/2nd day, assume model is overconfident; reduce first 5 days by 2–3%.
- If sentiment history shows strong bearish momentum (e.g., 3+ consecutive -1.00), model often underestimates; add 2–4% to forecast to avoid underreaction.
